newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to cuts benefits - deputy economy minister.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to cuts benefits - deputy economy minister.

text.p: Ukraine's deputy economy minister said on Wednesday that the government planned to cut some 16 billion hryvnias in citizen benefits from the 1997 budget, which is expected to be passed next month.
"Although most benefits are written into law, the government can no longer meet its obligations," Oleksander Yaramenko told a news conference.
Ukraine has tried to pay benefits to 51 million Ukrainians under a system inherited from the Soviet era, including subisidies for telephones, transport and energy bills.
"Just over one billion hryvnias go each year towards letting people ride on trolley buses at a reduced rate and the state covers medicines to the tune of 412 million hryvnias," Yaramenko said.
The government is expected to have problems getting the cuts past the largely conservative parliament, which is due to debate a budget that should have been passed by January 1.
Yaramenko said the government would try to find a way to ensure the growing number of people under the poverty line would not be adversely affected by the cuts.
"Whether we want to or not, we will be forced to implement these decisions," he said. "We expect parliament's support."
